current.text: He is a rookie. Atlanta drafted him 23rd in the 2026 NBA draft after his college career at St. John's.
He is a backup big man. Onyeka Okongwu is the projected starting center and Jock Landale is also on the center depth chart.
Lloyd expects a 10-man Hawks rotation, and Ejiofor is not in his list of bench players.
Atlanta's frontcourt depth is thin. Veesaar is out for the season, Gueye is injured, and power forward depth is bad to start the season.
His big college numbers as an upperclassman may not carry over to the NBA. One expert sees them as a red flag.
He could turn into a stretch big if his Summer League three-point shooting holds up.
In dynasty rookie rankings he is rank 25, tier 5.

durable.text: He is an undersized, switchy, high-energy big man.
He barely shot threes in college. In 2026 Summer League he took 52% of his shots from three and made 35% of them.
Projections give him very few threes, points and steals. His good FG% and low turnovers come on very small volume.

note: Ejiofor is not a draft option in our 144-player auction. Yahoo values him at 0 USD (rank 700), ESPN gives no price, and his Yahoo projection is only 5.0 points and 4.1 rebounds as a backup. Early in the season, watch two things. First, whether his Summer League three-point shooting carries into real minutes. Second, whether an injury to Okongwu or Jalen Johnson opens a role in Atlanta's thin frontcourt. Only then is he worth a waiver claim.
